definitions.gloss: stiff; hard; frozen up (with cold or tension)
definitions.explanation: Describes something rigid and hard—rock-frozen food, sun-baked clay, or a body stiff with cold or nerves. Also applies figuratively to inflexible people or attitudes.
The crisp ticking sound of a small clock or watch.

examples.japanese: {餅|もち}がコチコチに{凍|こお}っている。
{緊張|きんちょう}でコチコチに{固|かた}まっていた。
examples.english: I was frozen stiff with nervousness.

examples.japanese: {頭|あたま}がコチコチで{新|あたら}しいやり{方|かた}を{受|う}け{入|い}れようとしない。
examples.english: He's so rigid in his thinking that he refuses to accept new methods.

examples.japanese: {時計|とけい}がコチコチと{鳴|な}っている。
{夜中|よなか}、コチコチという{秒針|びょうしん}の{音|おと}だけが{聞|き}こえた。
examples.english: In the middle of the night, only the tick-tock of the second hand could be heard.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{壁掛|かべか}け{時計|どけい}がコチコチと{時|とき}を{刻|きざ}んでいる。
examples.english: The old wall clock is ticking off the seconds.

notes:
Sense 1 (stiff/rigid) is far more common in everyday speech and applies to both physical hardness and mental inflexibility. Sense 2 (ticking) is the original onomatopoeic meaning. Often written in katakana for emphasis.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- コチコチに{凍|こお}る: to freeze rock-hard
- コチコチに{固|かた}まる: to become stiff (with tension)
- {頭|あたま}がコチコチ: inflexible (in thinking)
- コチコチと{鳴|な}る: to tick

SIMILAR WORDS:
- カチカチ: harder, sharper sound; also "clicking" of teeth
- カチンコチン: emphatic form meaning "frozen solid"
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn — explicit description without the physical metaphor
